subject.title: feat(backup): add exclude patterns, --smart-exclude, and protected path guards [ai]

question: Should OpenClaw accept auto-loaded `.backupignore` plus warning-only external-asset excludes, or require an explicit opt-in exclude mode that applies uniformly to every planned backup asset before this PR continues?
rationale: This changes a restore-critical backup command and sensitive-data boundary, so automation should not decide the permanent UX/security policy for implicit ignore files or partial exclude semantics.

options.title: Require explicit and uniform excludes
options.body: Keep the feature direction but require explicit opt-in activation, per-asset filtering, protected restore paths, and live archive proof before merge.

options.title: Accept partial semantics intentionally
options.body: A maintainer may approve auto-loaded ignore files and warning-only external assets, but the behavior should be documented and treated as a deliberate compatibility/security tradeoff.

options.title: Pause or replace the branch
options.body: If the broad branch is not worth resolving, pause this PR and pursue a smaller maintainer-owned exclude implementation against current main.

recommendation.title: Require explicit and uniform excludes
recommendation.body: Keep the feature direction but require explicit opt-in activation, per-asset filtering, protected restore paths, and live archive proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent backup hardening and current-main path ownership make vincentkoc the best available routing candidate for the backup policy decision.
